scene.title: Global Electric Vehicle Industry
scene.subtitle: From a niche technology to roughly a quarter of new car sales

answer.headline: The global EV industry now sells around one in four new cars worldwide, led by Chinese manufacturers and anchored by falling battery costs.
body: What began as a small collection of compliance vehicles and early adopter products has grown into a manufacturing sector spanning battery cells, charging networks, and dozens of mainstream vehicle lines. China leads on both production and domestic sales, Europe leads on regulatory push, and the United States trails both but is closing the gap with new domestic battery plants.

The industry's next phase depends less on convincing buyers electric vehicles work and more on cost: battery pack prices, charging access outside major cities, and the used-vehicle market for older packs will decide how quickly the remaining three quarters of new car sales convert.
caveats: Figures blend battery-electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles unless noted otherwise.

scene.summary: The global EV industry covers battery-electric and plug-in hybrid vehicle manufacturing worldwide. It has grown from under 1% of new car sales in 2015 to roughly a quarter by 2025, led by Chinese manufacturers and falling battery costs.
